settingsPermissions.precedenceDescription: When more than one action-level rule covers the same action, the resolver keeps the strictest decision — deny outranks ask, and ask outranks allow. Rules with a command/path predicate are overrides: at call time the highest-priority matching rule decides (ties: deny > ask > allow), and with no match the action ladder decides.
settingsPermissions.actionsDescription: Every action the agent runtime can gate, and the decision resolvePermission produces for it under each shipped permission mode. This is the live resolver output, computed the same way the runtime computes it — both TDEaseNexus commands and Pi built-in tools go through the same resolver, not a separately stored setting. Workspace overrides are declared in .tdease/permissions.json.
settingsPermissions.workspaceDescription: Rules persisted in this workspace's .tdease/permissions.json (version 2). A rule may stay action-level — it tightens the Authority baseline, strictest decision wins — or carry a match: a command regex for bash, path globs for file tools, a priority, and a note shown on the approval card. The runtime re-reads the file whenever a session binds to the workspace.
settingsPermissions.workspaceNone: Open a workspace to manage its permission overrides.
settingsPermissions.rulesEmpty: No overrides — the Authority baseline above applies unchanged.
settingsPermissions.rulesSaved: Saved. The override takes effect the next time a session binds to this workspace.
settingsPermissions.bindNote: The preview evaluates the draft exactly as a bound session would — ladder first, then matching overrides by priority.
settingsPermissions.loadFailed: The existing permissions.json could not be read ({error}). Saving replaces it with the rules in this editor.
settingsPermissions.matchPathsPlaceholder: path globs — e.g. analysis/**, reports/*.md (empty = every path)
settingsPermissions.previewNote: First matching override wins; with none, the Authority ladder above decides. This is the runtime's own evaluator, not a re-implementation.
settingsPermissions.sandboxDescription: On macOS the agent's persistent bash is born inside a Seatbelt sandbox: writes are confined to the workspace and the OS temp area, everything else is read-only. On Linux the same box is provided by bubblewrap when it is installed. On Windows no OS sandbox is available yet — the path containment and the destructive-command blacklist remain the boundary there. The sandbox holds regardless of every permission decision above; it is defense in depth, not a fourth decision tier.
settingsPermissions.defaultPolicyNote: Ask authority ships a default review policy beneath your own rules: dangerous commands and credential paths are isolated outright, risky ones (recursive deletion, elevated execution, git push, package publish …) ask, and innocuous shell commands simply run. Your workspace rules and card approvals ("always allow") outrank it; Auto authority is unchanged, and the destructive-command guard holds in every mode.

settingsSharing.title: Workspace web sharing
settingsSharing.lead: Share in a browser: guests sign in with an access token and can watch the host's live AI conversation; the selected Workspace files stay available as a read-only view. Off by default; a token is generated before anything listens. Guests get no host credentials and cannot touch authorization settings.
settingsSharing.lanPlaintextWarning: LAN mode serves plaintext HTTP: the token, AI conversation and shared files cross your network unencrypted. Prefer loopback unless you trust the network.
